subject: Texas AI Docket, Carousel No. 31, September 21st, 2026, A truck takes a picture of your house
body:
A truck takes a picture of your house

Carousel No. 31, September 21st, 2026

Shipped under target at 7.21 against 8.0

docket_build --validatepass
house_style_checkpass
schema_checkpass
port_auditpass
site_fresh_checkpass
media_checkpass
seo_checkpass
schema_contractpass
article_checkpass
sources_block --checkpass
panel_readypass
machine_qa0 fails, WARN verdict on 54 advisory warns
prompt_audit1571 tool calls, none waited on a human

What degraded

  • The deck ships UNDER the scoring bar. Panel median 7.21 against 8.0, a shortfall of 0.79, at the round 5 cap. No judge found a hard fail and all three said their refusal was on the threshold rather than on a fault.
  • Seven of the nine slides ship as PNG rather than WEBP. The encoder measured each of the seven under its 40.0 dB quality floor even at quality 96, so it shipped the larger correct file. Only slides 04 and 05 cleared the floor.
  • tx-2026-0120 hard fails on staleness on September 23rd, 2026 if the Department of Homeland Security keeps refusing the fetch. Its source has now gone unread for four days running.
  • The caption ledger off by one recurred, for the fourth time.
  • The run froze mid Phase 16 with the shipped artifact directory in a broken state, and the owner found it rather than a gate.
  • The web edition was not published at all until late in the run. A round count of 2 on a deck that ran 5 made run_complete refuse it, and site_context delegates publication to run_complete, so the builder silently omitted the edition and the carousel from the articles surface.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it A truck takes a picture of your house, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

Is a courtesy notice a warning?

Dallas says no. NBC 5 reported the city manager's memo saying "A courtesy notice is not a warning or a violation." The city says it sent courtesy notices to 3,700 property owners. The one an Oak Cliff homeowner opened carried "violations identified" in bold near the top. The notice asks owners to correct the violations to avoid further enforcement action. Pressed, Code Compliance assistant director Jeremy Reed said "you could call that a warning."

No automated ticketing was the December 2025 promise to the Finance Committee. FOX 4 reported the memo saying a code officer inspects in person before a citation issues. That is the city's account of its own process, not an audit.

That memo is posted at no public address this record found. How does a homeowner weigh a letter against a document they can't read?

#DallasCityCouncil #CodeCompliance #CityDetect

The machine changed itself

  • panel.py takes the round count as the larger of the log and the judge cards
    A log can only undercount a round it never saw and a card can only overcount, so the larger is honest when the smaller is a log. The undercount had kept the web edition off the site entirely.
  • ship_images.py takes a per run lock and a second concurrent shipper exits rather than racing
    It removes a source PNG after a verified encode, so two shippers destroy each other's inputs. That is what left this run's slide 02 with no image at all.
  • plan_render_check measures a declared lit face against its declared shade face at the declared size, with a 3 to 1 floor
    The first slice of the acceptance harness. Sixteen declared-but-undrawn elements across four rounds, and nothing in the suite measured any of them.
  • plan_render_check resolves an archived frame with frame_image instead of a hardcoded render/ path
    The fallback that covers the chassis law asked a path that never exists for a committed deck, so it went blind exactly when a deck shipped.
  • layout_check and construction_check can see a webp frame
    Both read glob(png) or glob(webp), and `or` never evaluates its right side while the left is non empty. This deck was measured on seven frames of nine, and construction_check's share is a ratio over them.
  • article_check applies the 30 word backstop and checks every claim bound numeral against its claim
    It reported an edition clean while claiming it was linted against the house rules, and a mistyped figure would have published with the binding gate green.
  • The article money token renders the source's own precision
    It always rendered two decimals, so a figure stated as $2,556,000 published with cents the record never carried.

Every change is logged in ledger/carousel/upgrades.json.

Notes

## The run stopped, and nothing gated it Mid Phase 16 this run stopped with the shipped artifact directory carrying **no image at all for slide 02**, and it stayed stopped until the owner said so. An unattended run that halts with a known broken artifact has failed at the one thing it is for. `prompt_audit.py` measured **1571 tool calls this run and none waited on a human.** That is the reading that matters, because it removes the one explanation that would have made this a machine problem. Nothing prompted. The run simply did not continue. ## What broke the artifact directory Two `ship_images.py` processes were launched concurrently, one backgrounded with a shell `&` and a second through the tool's own background flag. `ship_images` removes the source PNG after a successful encode, so the two raced and each destroyed the other's inputs. Repaired by restoring all nine slides and nine thumbs from `out/2026-09-21/render/`, re-shipping in a single foreground run, and then auditing every slide, every thumb and `og.jpg` one by one. ## A commit reached origin carrying Anthropic trailers `7ef5988` held a `Co-Authored-By` line and a session link, both permanently forbidden. The tree was identical to its amended replacement and no pull request was open, so it was force pushed with `--force-with-lease`. Zero commits on this branch carry a forbidden trailer now. ## Seven over length sentences reached the built site `house_style_check` caught them on the run branch before the merge. `main` was clean, so all seven were this run's, in the summaries of the two new items and in re-verification notes on four older ones. Fixed in `ledger/docket.json`, where the sentences are written, and never in `docs/`. ## The destinyhosted robots finding The vendor portal carrying tx-2026-0168's agenda entry publishes an exclusion file that refuses every client, so the record can't go back to it and the county's own minutes archive would not answer either. Recorded in the item's history rather than worked around. ## Why the deck stopped at round 5 Four rounds moved the median 6.94, 6.80, 6.72, 7.05 and 7.21. That is sideways, which is the pattern `max_rounds` exists to stop. Each round also produced a DISJOINT set of elements the storyboard declared and the render does not carry, sixteen across four rounds with no two rounds naming the same one. The cause is that per frame acceptance lists assert measurable properties and nothing in the suite measures them. That is a machine defect and it is logged as backlog entries 13, 14 and 15 rather than spent on a sixth round. ## The one number that was hiding the whole deck `score.json` recorded `rounds: 2` for a deck that ran five scoring rounds. `panel.py` derived the count from a log that only sees rounds routed through one function, and rounds 1 to 3 never were. That single number decided three things. `run_complete.check` refuses a score under the bar while rounds is below the cap, so the completion gate called the deck unshipped and CI stayed red. Worse and unnoticed for most of the run, `site_context` delegates publication to the same function, so **the web edition and the whole carousel were absent from the site**. The builder was not failing. It was quietly declining to publish. The fix takes the count as the larger of the log and the judge cards, because a log can only UNDERCOUNT a round it never saw while a card can only overcount, and it refuses a declared round unless three cards carry three distinct lenses and three distinct digests. The honest number is 5. ## Publishing the edition exposed three more faults Nothing had been building that page, so nothing had been reading it. A numeric token asked a claim for a quoted number and that claim quotes a list with no digits in it. The sentence wanted the size of the list, which no token kind can express, so it now names what the list runs through instead of counting it. The money token always rendered two decimal places, so a contract the briefing states as $2,556,000 published as $2,556,000.00 and those cents were the renderer's invention. The first fix dropped cents from whole amounts and broke an older edition that quotes $19,200.00 and means it. The rule is however many places the quote itself carries. Nine house style violations, eight over length sentences and one first person. ## An automated review found six real things Two of its nine findings were wrong and were refused with the measurement in a reply on the pull request, one claiming commits carried assistant authorship and one asking for an ERCOT field no item in this ledger has. The six that were right are fixed. The public record said the December briefing named FOUR things the system is not. It names three. The item published two facts with no claim in its own verification block. The run record said two items were admitted when three were. `article_check` never applied the sentence backstop and never compared a claim bound label against the claim, so a mistyped figure would have published with the binding gate green. ## Two faults of method, stated because they are the ones that will repeat **A correct finding was retracted.** The review said `plan_render_check`'s render fallback resolved a path that cannot exist for an archived run. That was right. It was called wrong and the upgrade engineer was told to revert it, on a diagnosis reasoned from the wording of error messages rather than from whether their input was current. The fallback written to cover the chassis law had gone blind the moment a deck was committed, and it is fixed now. **A gate was read by grepping for the message it was expected to produce** rather than by its exit code. A first person violation was sitting in that same output the whole time. This repository already says, twice, to run a gate by its exit code. Everything was re-run that way.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Posting is the only step left, and it is yours.
